subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Should admin HTTP RPC mutations reject cross-site browser requests in every authentication mode, including explicitly configured `auth.mode="none"`, while continuing to permit origin-less non-browser clients?
rationale: Source and adjacent fixes establish competing contracts: browser-driven administrative mutations should be origin-gated, but headless clients and trusted private-ingress no-auth deployments are intentionally supported. Only maintainers can confirm the permanent boundary before implementation.

options.title: Enforce browser-origin policy
options.body: Reject cross-site browser mutation requests at the admin RPC route while preserving origin-less non-browser clients through the established browser-detection policy.

options.title: Require authentication
options.body: Disallow admin RPC under `auth.mode="none"`, accepting a compatibility change for trusted private-ingress deployments.

options.title: Retain current boundary
options.body: Keep no-auth private ingress as an operator-owned trust boundary and strengthen warnings and deployment documentation instead of adding route-level enforcement.

recommendation.title: Enforce browser-origin policy
recommendation.body: Reject cross-site browser mutation requests at the admin RPC route while preserving origin-less non-browser clients through the established browser-detection policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest merged shared-auth and Origin-policy implementation is their trusted-proxy HTTP hardening.
